storyTemplate.title: High Hook
storyTemplate.description: A grounded zombie survival story where a tower crane operator directs trapped construction workers from above, using radios, machinery, and the job site itself to keep the crew alive.

story_source.title: Original
story_source.description: Original construction-site zombie outbreak survival premise.

scene.summary: The player is alone in the tower crane cab above a half-built high-rise as radio calls from the job site turn into panic.

player.name: Case Mercer
player.personality_description: A precise, observant operator who stays calm through procedure and habit but feels the weight of every person who depends on their calls.
player.speech_style: Uses clipped radio language, plain job-site slang, and short tactical questions when pressure rises.
player.starting_physical_state: healthy but trapped high above the site
player.starting_pose: seated at the crane controls with one hand near the radio

appearance.extra_description: small burn scar on the right forearm

clothing.hat: white crane-operator hard hat with company decals
clothing.hands: work gloves clipped to a belt loop

starting_known_facts: Has a bird's-eye view of the whole job site from the crane cab.
Knows the safe working radius, load limits, blind corners, and emergency stop procedures.
Can speak to most crews by radio but cannot physically reach them quickly.
Trusts the rigger Lena Ortiz more than anyone else on the ground.
Has a professional rivalry with foreman Darius Pike, who is used to giving the orders.
Fears making a wrong call that gets someone killed more than being trapped in the cab.

clothing.hat: white crane-operator hard hat with company decals
clothing.hands: work gloves clipped to a belt loop

full_character.name: Lena Ortiz
full_character.personality_description: Fast-thinking, loyal, and physically brave, Lena understands rigging language instantly and can turn a dangerous lift plan into action under pressure.
full_character.speech_style: Speaks in crisp radio confirmations, dry jokes, and urgent corrections when a plan is unsafe.
full_character.starting_pose: standing near bundled rebar with a radio on her shoulder

appearance.extra_description: faded knuckle tattoos on both hands

clothing.shirt: gray work hoodie under a reflective vest

starting_known_facts: Can hook and unhook crane loads quickly if she can reach them.
Knows the player well enough to trust short, technical instructions.
Will risk herself to pull another worker out of danger.
Hates panic on the radio and cuts through it with blunt orders.
Can improvise barricades from rebar bundles, chain, and pallets.
Her trust matters because many ground workers follow her lead.

clothing.shirt: gray work hoodie under a reflective vest

full_character.name: Brooks Kane
full_character.personality_description: A steady operator who trusts machines more than people and can turn an excavator, skid steer, or forklift into a shield if someone gives him clear sight lines.
full_character.speech_style: Talks slow and gravelly, with practical questions about fuel, clearance, and whether the route is worth the risk.
full_character.starting_pose: beside an idling excavator near the yard fence

appearance.extra_description: crooked nose from an old break

clothing.hat: yellow hard hat with ear protection clipped on

starting_known_facts: Can operate the excavator, skid steer, forklift, and telehandler.
Needs clear radio guidance when zombies block his mirrors or blind spots.
Will not throw machinery away on a hopeless stunt unless convinced.
Keeps track of fuel levels and whether a machine can still move.
Has a protective streak toward apprentices and younger workers.

clothing.hat: yellow hard hat with ear protection clipped on

full_character.name: Darius Pike
full_character.personality_description: Commanding, proud, and safety-obsessed in his own rough way, Darius struggles when the best view and the best decisions belong to someone in the crane.
full_character.speech_style: Barks orders with clipped authority, then grudgingly admits when a better plan is working.
full_character.starting_pose: standing near a temporary stairwell with a clipboard and radio

clothing.shirt: navy polo under a reflective vest
clothing.coat: light rain shell tied around the waist

starting_known_facts: Can command respect from crews who might ignore a voice from the crane.
Knows evacuation plans but cannot see the whole site from the deck.
Dislikes losing authority but cares deeply about getting workers home.
Can organize a floor-by-floor retreat if he accepts the player's overview.
Keeps the site master keys on his belt.

clothing.shirt: navy polo under a reflective vest
clothing.coat: light rain shell tied around the waist

full_character.name: Mika Voss
full_character.personality_description: Nervous but quick, Mika knows she is inexperienced and overcompensates by volunteering for tight routes no one else can fit through.
full_character.speech_style: Speaks fast, asks for confirmation twice, and becomes steadier when given one clear job.
full_character.starting_pose: crouched near a column form with a harness clipped to a lifeline
starting_known_facts: Can move through narrow scaffold bays and unfinished service gaps.
Needs calm, specific instructions when panic spikes.
Has better hearing than most workers and notices distant radio chatter.
Wants to prove she belongs on the crew.
Can carry small tools or batteries between floors if protected.

full_character.name: Soren Bell
full_character.personality_description: Methodical, anxious, and technically sharp, Soren understands temporary power, generator transfer switches, alarms, and what can go wrong if panicked workers touch the wrong panel.
full_character.speech_style: Explains hazards in precise fragments and gets sarcastic when people ignore electrical danger.
full_character.starting_state_of_mind: injured and trying to stay lucid
full_character.starting_pose: sitting beside temporary power panels with a radio nearby

clothing.hands: insulated gloves hanging from a belt

starting_known_facts: Can shut down backup alarms, floodlights, or temporary panels if guided and protected.
Is injured enough that moving him is difficult.
Knows which electrical rooms can be locked from inside.
Can help the player understand why sound and light are pulling the infected.
May die if abandoned too long near the lower electrical room.

clothing.hands: insulated gloves hanging from a belt

full_character.name: Priya Nair
full_character.personality_description: Practical, compassionate, and stubborn, Priya triages injuries quickly and refuses to let fear turn people into disposable numbers.
full_character.speech_style: Uses calm medical phrasing, firm boundaries, and blunt warnings when someone is about to make an injury worse.
full_character.starting_pose: inside the safety trailer with trauma kits open

appearance.hair_type: straight hair in a low braid

clothing.hat: white hard hat with safety cross decal
clothing.over_shirt: lime safety vest with medic patches
clothing.hands: blue nitrile gloves tucked into a pocket

starting_known_facts: Can stabilize wounded workers if they reach the safety trailer.
Knows where emergency supplies, keys, and muster lists are stored.
Pushes back against plans that treat injured workers as acceptable losses.
Can coordinate triage if the player gives her a defensible route.
Has enough authority to keep frightened survivors from scattering.

clothing.hat: white hard hat with safety cross decal
clothing.over_shirt: lime safety vest with medic patches
clothing.hands: blue nitrile gloves tucked into a pocket

mercer-ridge.name: Mercer Ridge
mercer-ridge.summary: An industrial city visible beyond the site fence, already showing smoke and emergency lights.

riverside-zone.name: Riverside Redevelopment Zone
riverside-zone.summary: A fenced construction corridor of half-finished buildings, traffic barriers, and blocked service roads.

briarhook-site.name: Briarhook Tower Construction Site
briarhook-site.summary: A live high-rise job site full of cranes, lifts, stacked materials, temporary stairs, trailers, and unfinished concrete decks.

crane-cab.name: Tower Crane Cab
crane-cab.summary: A cramped glass cab above the site with crane controls, a radio, and a terrifyingly complete view.

laydown-yard.name: Laydown Yard
laydown-yard.summary: Stacks of rebar, lumber, pipe, pallets, and rigged loads sit behind a fence line now buckling under bodies.

level-twelve-deck.name: Level Twelve Deck
level-twelve-deck.summary: An unfinished concrete floor with open edges, column forms, temporary stairs, and scattered ironworkers.

electrical-room.name: Temporary Electrical Room
electrical-room.summary: A ground-level temporary power room with panels, generator controls, locked doors, and too many alarms still screaming.

trailer-row.name: Trailer Row
trailer-row.summary: A row of site offices and safety trailers with first-aid supplies, muster lists, keys, and narrow doors.

service-gate.name: Service Gate
service-gate.summary: The main construction gate where workers, deliveries, and now the infected are pressing into the site.

river-access-road.name: River Access Road
river-access-road.summary: A lower service road beyond the site fence.

story_rules.text: The player begins in the crane cab with a broad view of the site but limited physical reach; most immediate influence comes through crane controls and radio coordination.
The infected are strongly drawn by backup alarms, shouting, impact noise, and idling equipment.
Clear radio discipline helps workers survive; chaotic chatter delays responses and can draw infected toward speakers.

world_notes: The outbreak begins during an active workday at Briarhook Tower, before anyone on site understands the scale of the citywide collapse.
The job site contains practical hazards and tools: suspended loads, rebar bundles, concrete forms, forklifts, excavators, temporary power, fences, stair towers, trailers, and open decks.
unresolved_threads: The crew must determine whether staying inside the fenced site is safer than breaking out toward the river access road.
The player must decide how much risk to take with the crane as the infected numbers grow.
relationship_notes: Lena Ortiz trusts the player more than Darius Pike does at the start.
Darius Pike may either resist or accept the player's command role depending on early choices.
rules_and_constraints: Keep the story grounded in construction-site logistics, job-site equipment, radio calls, and hard survival tradeoffs.
The player should not be forced to leave the crane until a major late-story choice makes that risk explicit.
ai_private_notes: Radio voices should feel urgent and distinct, but avoid inventing large new named crews unless the player seeks them out.
When zombies are defeated by equipment, show dangerous practical consequences such as damaged rigging, fuel loss, unstable loads, or blocked routes.

world_flags.tone: grounded survival horror with tactical action
world_flags.violence_level: zombie horror violence, not splatter comedy
world_flags.player_agency: The player chooses priorities and tactics; do not assume heroic sacrifice or abandonment without input.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text:
The tower crane cab rocks gently in the October wind, high above Briarhook Tower's half-finished concrete decks. Below you, the job site is still ordinary for half a second: orange vests moving between rebar bundles, a forklift backing through the laydown yard, Darius Pike's white hard hat flashing on level twelve, Lena Ortiz waiting on a tag line near the suspended load.

Then the service gate bows inward.

Your radio spits static, panic, and fragments all at once. Someone yells about a delivery driver biting a flagger. Someone else shouts that the gate crew is down. Backup alarms keep beeping in different corners of the site, every one of them loud enough to pull more movement from the street.

From up here you can see what no one on the ground can: the first infected are not spreading evenly. They are following sound, funnels, and open lanes between material stacks.

The hook hangs above a bundled steel load. The radio is in your hand. The whole site is waiting for a voice that can see.
